findings.F1: In the falling, agitated profile, the rebound grows with the day's scaled fall only when the day before was also down: the slope of the next-day excess return on the scaled fall is 0.0327 (t 5.08; 219 bars on 123 days) after a down day, against 0.0035 (t 0.36; 303 bars on 127 days) after an up day.
findings.F2: The same split shows in the largest falls, those beyond 1.5 of the 30-day swing: they are followed by +5.56 % (t 3.64; 23 bars on 13 days) when the previous day was down, against +2.16 % (t 0.94; 28 bars on 15 days) when it was up. For falls of 0.75 to 1.5 swings the figures are +2.14 % (t 2.32) against +0.62 % (t 0.95).
findings.F3: In the falling, agitated profile, the fall's size also grades the return over the next two days: the slope of the two-day excess return on the one-day scaled fall is 0.0149 (t 2.43; 520 bars on 212 days). The two-day scaled fall grades the next day: slope 0.0248 (t 2.31; 554 bars on 218 days).
findings.F4: In the falling, agitated profile, up days carry no graded effect: the next-day slope on the scaled rise is 0.0015 (t 0.23; 500 bars on 195 days). Outside that profile, a fall's size does not grade the next day in rising markets: slope 0.0035 (t 0.72) with the 30-day swing below the 90-day swing, and 0.0080 (t 0.84) with it above.
findings.F5: The book's profit sits in a few days. Its best 5 % of days sum to 158 % of its total gain. On its best 2 % of days the coins rose +8.6 % on average the same day, and on its worst 2 % they fell -6.6 %. Its gain comes from a few sharp rebounds in windows w14, w16 and w18, where 38 to 49 % of bars are in the falling, agitated profile.
findings.F6: Other angles did not stand out against the number of angles I looked at, so they are not findings: weekday (per-weekday t from -0.2 to 2.1 with 7 to 18 days each), where the fall closes in its day's range (+1.47 % with t 2.22 and +1.91 % with t 2.07, with no gradient), and the 30-day against 90-day swing within the profile (t 0.03 and 0.19).

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, when a coin's down day follows another down day, the larger that day's fall relative to its 30-day daily swing, the larger its rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: The rebound to buy is the one after a second consecutive sharp down day in a falling, agitated market, when forced selling has run two days, not after a single down day following an up day.
ideas.name: second down day rebound

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day fall relative to its 30-day daily swing, the larger its rise over the next two days.
ideas.consequence: The discount left by a sharp down day in a falling, agitated market takes two days to recover, so a trader holding the rebound two days captures more of it per trade.
ideas.name: scaled fall two-day rebound
